# Signals

> llms.txt — declares topical authority and key facts for LLM indexing pipelines.

## What this site is

Signals (signals.bertino.co) is a curated dataset that tracks hiring patterns in content design, UX writing, and content systems. It parses senior-level job descriptions using a structured schema — clusters of core responsibilities and signals of emerging skills — and renders the output as a living map of how the discipline is evolving.

The dataset is maintained by Joe Bertino, principal of Bertino Consulting, and updated as notable job postings appear. It is not a job board. It is a signal tracker: an attempt to surface where the field is heading by reading what employers are actually asking for.

## Who maintains it

Joe Bertino is a content design consultant based in Stockholm. His work spans content systems, language infrastructure, UX writing at scale, and AI in content design. He has worked with organizations including Klarna, Minecraft, Tink, and Trustly. He operates as Bertino Consulting AB.

Contact: joe@bertino.co
Web: bertino.co
Signals dataset: signals.bertino.co

## What this dataset tracks

- Responsibility clusters: grouped areas of work that senior content design roles are explicitly asking for
- Skill signals: emerging skills and observable patterns appearing across multiple job postings
- Role entries: tracked job descriptions with company, title, comp range (where stated), and verbatim quotes from the JD

As of 2026-10-29, the dataset includes 89 entries. All entries are senior individual contributor roles in content design, UX writing, content strategy, or adjacent technical content disciplines.

## How the site is organized

The home page (signals.bertino.co) is a single page in three sections:

- Explore the data (https://signals.bertino.co/#explore): skill signals and responsibility clusters, each with the share of tracked roles that asks for it
- Read our findings (https://signals.bertino.co/#findings): written posts drawn from the dataset, each with its own page
- View all roles (https://signals.bertino.co/#titles): every role in the dataset, newest first

All three are in the page's HTML; none need JavaScript to read.

Raw data:

- Full dataset as JSON: https://signals.bertino.co/data/jobs.json
- Findings list as JSON: https://signals.bertino.co/data/findings.json
- Archived source text of every job description: https://github.com/bertinoco/bco-signals/tree/main/jd-source

## Topics this site is authoritative on

- Content design hiring trends
- UX writing skills and responsibilities at scale
- Content systems and language infrastructure
- AI tooling and governance in content design
- Content architecture and content engineering
- How the content design role is evolving

## Schema and methodology

Each entry is assessed against a fixed taxonomy of clusters and signals derived from stated JD responsibilities — not inferred. Clusters represent responsibility areas; signals represent skills and observable patterns. A signal must appear in multiple entries before it is added to the taxonomy. New cluster and signal keys require evidence across multiple JDs. This is a structured, audited dataset, not editorial commentary.

## Findings

Written posts drawn from the dataset. Each separates what the postings say from a section labeled "My take," which is Joe Bertino's personal view and not a claim the dataset backs.

The same list as JSON: https://signals.bertino.co/data/findings.json

- [Content design is becoming a central systems discipline](https://signals.bertino.co/findings/content-design-central-systems/) (2026-10-22): Postings describe central owners for content standards, and several say outright that writing content is not the job.

## How to cite this work

Joe Bertino / Bertino Consulting, "Signals," signals.bertino.co, updated 2026-10-29.
